rationale: A wins because it stays inside the evidence and turns uncertainty into proof requirements instead of smuggling it into the headline. Its “A state fire agency signed an MOU with a satellite startup that hasn't launched anything” is a clean, reportable tension; B's “agencies are signing before the hardware exists” turns one unnamed MOU into a trend. B has sharper proof asks in places, but it keeps borrowing facts it was not given, and that is how a pitch becomes a correction.
gaps_in_A: “Story type: trend” on the MOU angle is overstated. One unnamed state-agency MOU is a procurement/customer story until Helio can show a pattern.
“says something about how desperate agencies are for faster detection” is plausible, but not proven. Keep it as a question, not a claim.
A misses a kept skeptical technical angle around “minutes” despite correctly refusing the overclaim. A reporter may make the claim itself the story.
“June sits inside the Northern Hemisphere fire season” is careful enough, but still a soft peg. It should not carry any pitch without a live policy, budget, or agency signal.
gaps_in_B: “before a lookout tower does” invents the comparison baseline. The update says faster than current systems, not which systems.
“two people from those exact companies” invents founder count and résumé mapping. The update only says founders are ex-SpaceX and ex-Planet Labs.
“agencies are signing before the hardware exists” turns one MOU into a plural market pattern. That is not an angle; that is a fact-check failure wearing a blazer.

“the current detection stack is failing them” and “prevailing belief this cuts against is real and currently loud” are unsupported zeitgeist claims. If you need outside context, say you need it; don't conjure it.
